name: Tharcon
description: Tharcon is a selective attentional suppression compound that works by chemically downregulating the brain's peripheral processing networks while amplifying activity in threat-assessment and target-acquisition pathways. The user's perception of the world narrows to a functional combat frame — non-threats become background noise, movement draws immediate attention, and decision latency on threat/non-threat classification drops to near-zero. Helix designed it for military snipers and close-protection operatives who need to remain lethal in complex, high-civilian environments.
effects: Radical narrowing of attentional focus to threat-relevant stimuli
Suppression of distracting environmental noise (emotional, sensory)
Enhanced target tracking in complex visual environments
side_effects: Complete inability to process non-threat information — users miss critical contextual data
High civilian casualty risk due to simplified threat classification
Users become vulnerable to threats they have not pre-classified
Tunnel vision becomes literal at high doses — peripheral vision loss
Disorientation in low-threat environments as brain struggles to expand processing
Emotional dissociation from victims — documented in post-op trauma reports
cultural_context: Tharcon is technically military-only, but it leaks — it always leaks, because the people who have access to it understand its value and the people who want it on the Shelf will pay premium prices. In GLMZ combat culture, Tharcon is respected and feared in equal measure: respected because it makes a competent shooter terrifyingly effective, feared because it makes an incompetent one a mass casualty event. There are verified incidents where Tharcon-dosed security personnel opened fire in public spaces because a non-combatant moved in a way that triggered threat classification.
story_hooks: A massacre at a Tier 2 market is being investigated — witnesses describe the shooter moving with inhuman precision and ignoring screaming civilians as if they weren't there; Tharcon is the obvious explanation but someone with military access supplied it.

A runner is offered a Tharcon vial for a precision extraction job and must decide whether the tactical advantage is worth operating with a perception that will make everyone around her a potential target.

Helix Biosystems has developed a civilian variant of Tharcon marketed as a 'productivity focus aid' — it is less potent but the threat-classification narrowing is still present, and white-collar users are beginning to exhibit troubling behavioral patterns.
